Rehabilitation of Mined Lands
All reclamation and revegetation procedures will be conducted in compliance with the Montana Strip Mining and Reclamation Act (Chapter 325), pursuant to Rules and Regulations, and Guidelines issued by the Montana Department of State Lands, as well as applicable federal regulations. There will undoubtedly be changes and modifications in these reclamation methods as the art of reclamation progresses.
Reclamation of mined land begins with the stripping of the topsoil before actual mining begins. The topsoil will be removed to a depth determined by soil survey and chemical analysis. In most cases, topsoil will include the "A", "B" and "C" horizons, provided chemical tests indicate that these materials constitute a desirable medium for plant growth. Where possible, the topsoil will be hauled directly to recontoured spoils to eliminate double handling of the material and deterioration of the topsoil through possible adverse effects on soil microganisms and death of vegetative matter (roots, rhizomes and seeds) in stockpiles.
Recontouring of spoil piles will be carried on concurrently with strip mining operations, a minimum of two spoil piles behind the actual mining operation. Bulldozers and scrapers are used to reduce the spoil piles to grades not greater than 1 vertical unit to 5 horizontal (about 11.5 degrees). An exception to this may be the final highwall which may have a slope as great as 1:3, or about 19.5 degrees.
